paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this one. A widow with one jar of oil and a woman with a son who has died both end up in places they can't fix on their own. Neither one has a plan that works. Both bring what they have and what they can't handle to the man of God, and the LORD meets them there (2 Kings 4:2, 4:27).

Look at the Shunammite woman. When her husband asks why she's going, she says, "Everything is all right." When she reaches Elisha, she clings to his feet, and he says her soul is in deep distress (2 Kings 4:23, 4:27). I think the lesson is that you don't have to dress up your pain before you bring it. She wasn't tidy or calm, and she still got a hearing. She also said, "I will not leave you," and she meant it (2 Kings 4:30).

So here's what to carry out of my bakery. Bring the small jar and the broken heart to the LORD, and keep bringing them, even when you can't see how He'll answer. The widow's oil kept flowing until the jars ran out, and the boy who had died opened his eyes (2 Kings 4:6, 4:35). I know a little about being stuck in the dark, friend, and I'm telling you, God isn't intimidated by your empty jars.
